3-wp6330-21c.doc Date : 20Th February, 2023.
Both the Writ Petitions were on board on 17th January, 2023 to enable the State Government to make a statement about the progress, if any, in appointment of the Competent Authority.
Both the matters are on today's board for directions.

Learned Advocate General for the State Government states that the Competent Authority is already appointed at Aurangabad for hearing the reference under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: He further states on instructions that he will make an endeavour to set up the Competent Authority insofar as Amravati Division and Nashik Division is concerned within six weeks from today.
We direct the State Government to set up the Competent Authority at Amravati Division and Nashik Division within eight weeks from today, without fail.
2. Learned Advocate General further states that considering the number of references at Konkan Division at 179 and Pune Division at less than 500.

The Competent Authority would be appointed for Nashik Division and would be directed to hold circuit hearings at Konkan Division and Pune Division depending upon the number of references pending before the Konkan Division as well as 3-wp6330-21c.doc Pune Division.
A chart tendered across the bar shows the comparison of Konkan Division and Pune Division.
In Pune Division, about 393 references are pending and to be heard by the Competent Authority.
The Competent Authority to have more sittings at Nashik Division and Pune Division depending upon the pendency.

3. Mr.Potnis, learned counsel for the Petitioners in Writ Petition No.6330 of 2021 invited our attention to an affidavit in reply filed by the State Government in Writ Petition No.3394 of 2019 and submitted that since the references pending at Pune Division are more than 500, which are to be heard by Collector and Competent Authority, there should be a separate Competent Authority for Pune Division.

Dr.Saraf, learned Advocate General for the State Government states that at this stage,
the State Government would appoint the Competent Authority at Nashik Division which would also be dealing with the references pending at Konkan Division and Pune Division and would consider setting up separate Competent Authority for Pune Division in near future depending upon the disposal of the references by the Competent Authority which would be appointed for Nashik Division.
Statement is accepted.

sentences.text: The State Government to review the position for separate Competent Authority at Pune Division after six months of the setting up of the Competent Authority at Nashik Division depending upon the 3-wp6330-21c.doc pending references to be heard by the Competent Authority.

5. Mr.Kapse, learned counsel for High Court made a suggestion that instead of giving two months time to the State Government to set up the Competent Authority at Amravati Division and Nashik Division, less time should be granted, in any event before 31st March, 2023 with a view that the budget earmarked for the financial year 2022-2023 is available for setting up of the two posts of the Competent Authority and if the time is granted beyond 31st March, 2023, budget otherwise available for the financial year 2022-2023 shall get lapsed and, in that event, the State Government would not be able to appoint the Competent Authority in view of the funds not being available earmarked in budget for 2023-24.
In our view, the suggestion given by Mr.Kapse, learned counsel for High Court is reasonable.
6. We have granted eight weeks time with a mandatory direction to the State Government to appoint the Competent Authority so as to obviate the request for extension of time after expiry of six weeks.

It is made clear that the State Government shall earmark funds in the budget for the financial year 2023-2024, if required and for setting up a Competent Authority for Pune and other Divisions so that there would not be any impediment for the purpose of setting up of the Competent Authority within eight weeks.

The 3-wp6330-21c.doc State Government would provide budgetary provision for setting up of the Competent Authority in future if any decision is taken by the State Government on its own or if directed by this Court to the State Government.

7. We accept the assurance given by the learned Advocate General that the Competent Authority would be set up as directed above within the time prescribed so as to mitigate the hardship caused to the litigants, whose references are pending and would be filed.
8. Place both the Writ Petitions on board under the caption of directions for reporting compliance on 2nd May, 2023.

(M.M. SATHAYE , J.) (R.D. DHANUKA, J.)
